analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a decent consumer electricals franchise with a recognisable brand across fans, pumps, and appliances, but its 9.8% 7-year revenue CAGR and 8.2% profit CAGR fall well short of the 20-30% growth pace I require. Net profit in FY25 (INR 564 Cr) is still below FY21 levels (INR 617 Cr), which is simply not the compounding engine I seek.
key_strengths: Near-zero debt (D/E 0.05) with 5/5 years of positive OCF, providing financial resilience
Expanding revenue from INR 4,080 Cr (2018) to INR 7,864 Cr (2025) shows steady market penetration in fans and pumps
DII holding of 65.73% signals strong domestic institutional conviction; positive EBITDA trend recovering to INR 950 Cr in FY25
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 9.8% over 7 years — half of my minimum growth threshold
Net profit declined from INR 617 Cr (FY21) to INR 476 Cr (FY23) and only partially recovered to INR 564 Cr (FY25), indicating structural margin pressure post-Butterfly acquisition
Operating margin of just 7.99% leaves little room for competitive pricing or R&D reinvestment — a consumer durables company without wide margins rarely builds a durable moat
red_flags: Finance costs spiked to INR 109 Cr in FY23 from INR 35 Cr in FY22, driven by acquisition leverage for Butterfly Gandhimathi — integration risk and earnings dilution still visible
Forward P/E of 27x for a sub-10% revenue grower with declining net profit over 4 years is stretched
No visible R&D investment or proprietary technology pipeline — competing largely on brand and distribution, not innovation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crompton operates in a large, competitive consumer durables market where fans and pumps are semi-commoditised. The Butterfly acquisition in FY22 added kitchen appliances but simultaneously loaded the balance sheet with ~INR 1,686 Cr of debt and lifted finance costs sharply; debt has since been reduced to INR 186 Cr in FY25, which is commendable, but the profit trajectory was clearly damaged. For a Fisher-type investment I need to see a company developing genuinely new products with expanding addressable markets — Crompton's product roadmap looks evolutionary rather than revolutionary.

The fundamental problem is the growth rate. From my scuttlebutt lens, the fans market is mature, and while premiumisation in ceiling fans and solar pumps offers some upside, these are incremental opportunities. ROE of 17.4% is acceptable but below my 20% threshold, and with margins stuck around 8%, there is limited earnings leverage on incremental revenue. This is a reasonable business at a reasonable price, not the exceptional company I hunt.
